overview: Harlyn Bay is a big, family-friendly beach about three miles from Padstow, popular for surfing and well suited to beginners. With lifeguards in season, toilets, cafés and parking near the sand, it’s an easy north-coast beach day.
It has a surprising past: in 1865 a labourer found two thin crescents of Bronze Age gold, called lunulae, here, and there are several prehistoric sites around the bay.

expect.title: Surf for beginners
expect.text: A family and surfing beach that suits people learning to surf.

expect.title: Coast path
expect.text: The South West Coast Path links Harlyn with Mother Ivey’s Bay, Trevose Head and the beaches beyond, and east to Trevone.

goodToKnow.label: Where it is
goodToKnow.text: About three miles from Padstow and a mile from St Merryn.

week.text: A good choice for a first surf lesson near Padstow. It faces north, so it can be cooler and breezier on some days; on those, try a south-facing beach instead.

pairWith.why: a sandy cove a short walk east
a quieter bay to the west

tips: Book a surf lesson in advance in the school holidays.
